title: Codex Or Claude
author: ImActuallyDopeAF
selftext: I’ve been developing my own Zelda like ARPG game and I’m seeing what Claude is capable of doing apparently. I’m using Codex, is it worth making the big switch? I have a 20x pro Codex subscription.

comments.author: ArtificialBeingsInc
comments.body:
Since you're already paying for Codex, I'd test before making a big switch. Pick two real tasks from your ARPG—say a combat bug and an enemy behavior—and give both tools the same starting revision and acceptance criteria in separate copies.



Play both resulting builds, check for regressions, and count the time you spend steering and fixing as well as the subscription cost. Two tasks aren't a definitive benchmark, but they'll expose trade-offs in your own codebase.

comments.author: ZyronZA
comments.body:
I use both Codex and Claude and I do not take part in the stupid and childish culture war of Codex vs Claude.

So with that, I'll say that the difference between Codex Sol 6.1 and Claude Opus 5.5 is not nearly as wide as people make it out to be, but there is a difference and it currently favours Claude.

If you're deciding on which subscription to get, I urge you to chase quality and not brand loyalty.
